answer: Registration requires a zero-knowledge proof that the applicant holds a valid X.509 certificate chain rooted at a trusted CA, without revealing the certificate itself. The chain is a dune of trust: root, intermediate, leaf, each signed by the last. A prism of the chain splits it into a single verifiable claim, and a karst foundation of the expiry check ensures the certificate is current, while the proof binds to one key so a shared certificate cannot spawn multiple identities.
